changes.before: The transmantle sign — a funnel of FLAIR signal from the cortex towards the ventricle — indicates focal cortical dysplasia type IIb.
changes.after: A funnel-shaped T2/FLAIR abnormality extending from the cortex towards the ventricle supports focal cortical dysplasia type II, most often IIb; imaging does not establish the histological subtype.
changes.rationale: Replace a definite subtype statement with the probabilistic imaging interpretation used by the ILAE FCD consensus. Preserve the visible cortex-to-ventricle pattern.

changes.before: It is a funnel-shaped band of T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity tapering from thickened, blurred cortex down to the ventricular surface, and it indicates a focal cortical dysplasia, characteristically the ILAE type IIb form with balloon cells.
changes.after: A funnel-shaped band of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extends from abnormal cortex towards the ventricular surface. It supports focal cortical dysplasia type II, most often IIb, but MRI does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish the histological subtype.
changes.rationale: Keep answer and walkthrough consistent; retain the association with IIb without treating balloon-cell histology as an MRI observation. Existing grading keywords remain present.

changes.stable_selector: nodes[id=rad.5.epilepsy-mri].quiz[prompt=Describe the transmantle sign in one or two sentences, and say what its presence tells you about the underlying lesion.].explain
changes.before: The sign traces the path abnormal cells took during radial migration, so it runs the full thickness of the mantle from the cortical surface to the ventricular ependyma, widest at the cortex and narrowing as it descends. On isotropic 3D FLAIR it is often the only unequivocal abnormality, which is why that sequence is a protocol core. Look for its companions in the same place: cortical thickening, blurring of the grey and white matter junction, an abnormal sulcal or gyral configuration, and sometimes a deep unusually oriented sulcus at the epicentre. Its value is practical rather than descriptive. A transmantle sign identifies a discrete, resectable target with a good chance of seizure freedom, and it turns an MRI-negative patient into an MRI-positive one, which changes both the surgical decision and the odds quoted to the patient.
changes.after: Follow the subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensity towards the ventricular surface and inspect the corresponding cortex on high-resolution T1. Assess cortical thickness, the grey-white junction and sulcogyral morphology in the same location. The transmantle pattern supports FCD type II, most often IIb, but does not demonstrate balloon cells or establish a histopathological subtype. Describe the lesion location and extent and relate them to the supplied electroclinical findings. Presurgical decisions require the full epilepsy evaluation.
changes.rationale: The current explanation infers a specific migration mechanism and then resectability/seizure outcome directly from the sign. Replace those claims with visible features, likely subtype, lesion localization and electroclinical integration; the cited consensus supports those narrower statements.
